explain.say: Have you ever had money at the start of the month and none by the middle? A budget fixes that. A budget is a plan for your money: what comes in and where it goes. Look at the checklist: six steps to a budget that works.

Finally, check each week and adjust if you overspend. Great planning! Wow: many grown-ups use the 50-30-20 idea: 50 percent for needs, 30 for wants and 20 for saving. Try it on your own money!

faq.a: Income is all the money coming in, such as pocket money, gifts, or pay for chores. For adults it includes wages and other earnings.
A budget is a plan for your money that lists what comes in and decides where it will go, so you do not run out.
Any amount helps, but a common goal is between a tenth and a quarter of what you get. Saving one quarter of 200 is 50 a month, or 600 in a year.
asks: What share of money should I save?

faq.q: What if I spend more than I planned?
faq.a: Do not worry; just look at where the money went, cut back on wants next week, and change the plan if it was unrealistic. Budgets get better with practice.
It is a simple budget guide: about 50 percent of income for needs, 30 percent for wants and 20 percent for saving. It was made popular by Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi in 2005.
asks: How should I split my money?

facts: One quarter of 200 is 50; saving 50 a month gives 600 in a year.
The 50/30/20 budget idea was popularised in the 2005 book All Your Worth.
